nodes.summary: Nondeterministic choice is safe exactly when both branches are.
nodes.title: Hoare rule for nondeterministic choice

nodes.summary: Strengthen the precondition and weaken the postcondition.
nodes.title: Hoare rule of consequence

nodes.summary: Formula assertions connect Hoare verification to global PDL validity, not just an atomic-action modality.
nodes.title: Hoare triples with formula assertions as box validity

nodes.summary: Partial correctness agrees with the canonical relation's core.
nodes.title: Partial correctness as inclusion in the relational core

nodes.summary: The equivalent KAT absorption equation for verification.
nodes.title: Hoare triples as KAT absorption equations

nodes.summary: Hoare verification is equivalent to the KAT test inequality.
nodes.title: Hoare triples as KAT test inequalities

nodes.summary: Every execution of `a` from `P` ends in `Q`, without a termination requirement.
nodes.title: Partial-correctness Hoare triple for PDL programs

nodes.summary: PDL induction restricted to states reachable from the initial world. This proves `[a*](φ → [a]φ) → (φ → [a*]φ)` without assuming preservation on unreachable states.
nodes.title: PDL induction restricted to reachable states

nodes.summary: Sequential verification uses the first postcondition as the second precondition.
nodes.title: Hoare rule for sequential composition

nodes.summary: A one-step invariant holds after every finite number of iterations, including zero, via CSLib's canonical closure-preservation theorem.
nodes.title: Hoare invariant rule for iteration

nodes.summary: A formula test requires the postcondition only where the test passes.
nodes.title: Hoare rule for formula tests

nodes.summary: Concrete relational test absorption lifts through PDL iteration, connecting the algebraic verification equation to closure invariance.
nodes.title: Test absorption lifts through iteration

nodes.summary: A guarded-body verification equation implies the loop's exit verification equation over the same canonical relational carrier.
nodes.title: Loop exit absorption from a guarded-body absorption equation

nodes.summary: The guarded-loop invariant rule is partial correctness, including zero-step exits; it does not guarantee termination.
nodes.title: Hoare invariant rule for guarded while loops

nodes.summary: Verify a guarded loop using initialization, invariant preservation, and the exit implication to the desired postcondition.
nodes.title: While-loop rule with initialization and exit implication

nodes.summary: The guarded-loop rule is semantically complete for arbitrary set assertions. The witness is guarded-body reachability from `P`, independent of `Q`; this is not a completeness claim for a syntactic assertion language.
nodes.title: Semantic completeness of the while-loop invariant rule

nodes.summary: A guarded loop in the existing PDL syntax: iterate guarded body steps, then test that the guard is false.
nodes.title: Guarded while loop in PDL

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
